Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:38: Regarding something similar, they explained in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, parashah 29:7), in these words: Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina, he opened, "thus says the Lord your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord your God, who teaches you to profit" (Isaiah 48:17) — He goads you as one goads this cow with a goad. It is called by three names: "melamed" [teacher], "marde'a" [goad], "darban" [prod]. "Melamed" — for it teaches the cow to plow so that it give life to its owner; "marde'a" — for it instructs [morah da'at] the cow; "darban" — for it gives understanding [morah binah] to the cow. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: if a person makes a goad for his cow, how much more so for his own evil inclination, which removes him from the life of this world and the next! — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:39: Whoever accustoms himself to the pleasures of the world from his youth ends up unable to separate from them, as Solomon the king, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 29:21), "he who pampers his servant from youth, in the end he will become a master" — and his "servant" is the evil inclination, in the manner explained in the Zohar (parashat Toldot 144b), "better one who is lightly esteemed and has a servant" (ibid. 12:9). And whoever nullifies his desires and pleasures for the sake of the Creator's will, the possessors of judgment, as well as the accusers, are nullified from before him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:40: Of this the Mishnah says (Avot 2:4), "nullify your will before His will, so that He nullify the will of others before your will" — and the intent is this: a person's natural will and inclination is to be drawn after worldly desire, in eating and drinking, and to sleep the whole night, and other such things — but His will, blessed be He, is not so, but rather that we be sanctified, as we say every day twice in the Shema, "and you shall be holy to your God" — for it is impossible for us to be bound to Him unless He is called "your God," and this comes only through holiness; and when a person nullifies his will and nature for the sake of His will, blessed be He, the Holy One, blessed be He, nullifies the will of others, who are the outside forces drawn from another god called "other gods," whose will is always to arouse judgment and accusation against man — and since man has nullified his nature for the will of the Creator, and the world was created according to its nature, which is Elohim, for "teva" [nature] has the same numerical value as "Elohim," so too those forces called "others," all of which are drawn from judgment, are all nullified — on the contrary, they are subdued to become like servants under their masters, as we find in the Gemara (Chullin 105b) several stories where demons were subdued before the sages and served them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:41: It is also possible to allude to what they said in Bereishit Rabbah (67:3): six things serve man, three within his control and three not within his control — and we quoted his words in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 18. And it says at the end of the passage: at a time when a person is meritorious, the Holy One, blessed be He, makes those [three normally] not within his control [come] within his control — the mouth: "also, he shall be blessed" (Genesis 27:33); the hand: "and his hand dried up," etc. (I Kings 13:4) — and this is exactly "nullify the will of others" that are within their own control, "before your will" — this is the aspect of negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:42: Corresponding to the aspect of positive commandments, it precedes and says "do His will as your own will" — for just as a person derives satisfaction when his own commands are fulfilled, so the Holy One, blessed be He, although He needs nothing from any of those below, His will is that we serve Him, so that it be good for us — this being "so that He do your will as His will," for His simple will is to do good and have mercy, as the prophet said (Isaiah 60:10), "for in My wrath I struck you, and in My favor I had mercy on you." However, we must have the readiness within us to receive His goodness, in the manner explained in the Zohar as "arousal from below," as they proved from the verse "I am my beloved's," which we quoted above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:43: The pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz wrote close to what we have written regarding "so that He nullify the will of others." And regarding "do His will as your own will," he was precise in noting that it does not say "do His commandment," to indicate the aspect of holiness, that His will, blessed be He, is that we be sanctified, in the manner explained by the Ramban (beginning of parashat Kedoshim), which we quoted in the Gate of Holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:44: The things needed to do on a fast day in order to lighten the distress are all the things in which "life" [chayim] is mentioned; the reason being that since on the fast day one's fat and blood are diminished, the power of vitality within them is also melted and diminished — therefore one must engage in everything in which "life" is mentioned in Torah and Prophets, whatever is a commandment to do, for through this the soul shines more, and from that illumination gives a power of vitality to the limbs of the body. Moreover, we already find the term "life" used for healing, in the manner of (Joshua 5:8), "and they remained in their places in the camp until they were healed [chayotam]"; "and they applied it to the boil, and he recovered [vayechi]" (Isaiah 38:21); and likewise (Leviticus 13:16), "the raw [living] flesh."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:45: The first thing, which encompasses all the things in which "life" is mentioned in Torah and Prophets, is repentance — in the Torah, in the manner of (Deuteronomy 33:6), "let Reuben live and not die" — and it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayeshev 185b) that because Reuben strove to keep Joseph alive, to save him, "life" is mentioned regarding him, and likewise because he performed repentance, in these words: and because he performed repentance from that deed, and whoever performs repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, sustains him in this world and in the World to Come. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:46: In the Book of Ezekiel, "life" is mentioned several times regarding the penitent, particularly in this verse (33:15), where "life" is mentioned doubled: "if the wicked restore the pledge, repay what he has robbed, walk in the statutes of life, committing no iniquity, he shall surely live, he shall not die." And they said in Yoma (86b): Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan, great is repentance, for it lengthens a person's days and years, as it is said, "he shall surely live." — end of quotation. And repentance is in the examination of one's deeds, the abandonment of sin, and the other conditions explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:47: The second matter of warning in which "life" is mentioned is guarding the tongue, as it is written (Psalms 34:13), "who is the man who desires life... guard your tongue from evil." We have already explained in the Gate of Holiness, in the name of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the explanation of "from evil" means from sufferings — for one who sins with his tongue, sufferings come upon him, in the manner Rashi explained (Avot 1:17), "I have found nothing better for the body than silence."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:48: It is further explained in the Tikkunim (111a), in these words: further, "the sun rises and the sun sets" (Ecclesiastes 1:5) — this is the Holy One, blessed be He, wherever the Shechinah is with Him, in the manner of (Exodus 20:21), "in every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned" — Onkelos translates: in the place where the Shechinah shall rest there — and if the Shechinah is not there, "and the sun sets" — the Holy One, blessed be He, gathers Himself away from him, and he remains in darkness, and several destroyers and several evil sufferings rule over him, which are not sufferings of love — this being what is written (Deuteronomy 31:17), "is it not because my God is not within me that these evils have found me" — for these evils are from Him at every time and moment, of which it is said (Job 7:18), "and You visit him every morning, and test him every moment" — and what causes the Shechinah not to rest upon him and the sun not to shine upon him? Because of the breath of falsehood and words of falsehood that emerge from his mouth. And therefore (Ecclesiastes 8:14), "there is a vanity [hevel] that is done on the earth" — there is one kind of "hevel" and another kind of "hevel" — there is "hevel" of the masters of falsehood, of whom it is said (Jeremiah 10:15), "they are vanity, a work of delusion," for they err in the vanity of falsehood; and there is "hevel" of which it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3), "for by every utterance of the mouth of YHVH does man live" — this is the "hevel" [breath] of Torah, which is heh, the five books of the Torah, from the bet of "Bereishit" to the lamed of "le-einei kol Yisrael" ["before the eyes of all Israel," the last words of the Torah] — and this is "heB"L" [breath/vanity]. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:49: Here, evil breath removes the Shechinah and the Holy One, blessed be He, from man, and then sufferings rule over him; but the breath of Torah is not so — rather, it brings life to man, as it says, "for by every utterance of the mouth of YHVH does man live." Whoever wishes to be bound to his God should reduce speech even in matters he needs, and increase silence, as explained in the verse (Psalms 34:13), "who is the man who desires life," for the essence of life is clinging, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are alive" — and "guard your tongue from evil" is explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:50: Further, in the Book of Ezekiel (18:5), "and a man who is righteous and does justice and righteousness, who has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, nor defiled his neighbor's wife, nor approached a woman in her menstrual impurity, and has not wronged any man, has restored the debtor his pledge, has robbed no one by violence, has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with a garment, has not given upon interest, nor taken increase, has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, has executed true judgment between man and man, has walked in My statutes and kept My judgments, to deal truly — he is righteous, he shall surely live."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:51: Further, one should be careful in the aspects of good fear explained in the Gate of Fear, of which Solomon said (Proverbs 10:27), "the fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened," and likewise (ibid. 14:27), "the fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death." And to guard the disciplines of Torah, as it is written (ibid. 4:13), "take hold of discipline, do not let go; guard it, for it is your life," and it says (ibid. 10:17), "he who guards discipline is in the path of life, but he who forsakes rebuke goes astray."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:52: Further, it is fitting that he rise early for the synagogue to be counted among the first ten, which our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 8a) lengthens one's days, and they proved this from the verse (ibid. 8:35), "for whoever finds Me finds life." This aspect is especially efficacious, particularly if he is the first, provided he prays in that same synagogue where he was among the first ten — and so I received from the mouth of my master, may his rest be in Eden, that the reward our sages, of blessed memory, mentioned for coming among the first ten applies only to one who prays there, and this is also evident from the words of the Zohar in parashat Naso.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:53: Also a great assistance for the penitent is to be helped by the Creator by day, if he rose early to read Torah and to pray over his sins, as it is written (Psalms 88:2), "O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cry out, and at night before You" — and we have elaborated on this in the Gate of Holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:54: Further, he should be careful regarding the commandment of tefillin, explained as lengthening the days of one who dons them, as it is written (Isaiah 38:16), "O Lord, by these things men live" — so our sages, of blessed memory, said in Menachot (44b). A penitent should have two pairs — one according to Rashi's view, peace be upon him, and one according to Rabbeinu Tam's view, peace be upon him — and during the morning prayer he should put on both pairs in order to fulfill the commandment of reciting Shema properly, so that he not be said to bear false witness against himself, since one pair's tefillin are invalid according to the other view, and it would follow that he recited the Shema without [valid] tefillin according to one opinion; and for the rest of the day he should wear the tefillin according to Rabbeinu Tam's view, and whenever his body is found clean he should wear them and find himself helped by the Creator — for they said there, in the chapter HaTechelet, Rav Sheshet said, whoever does not don tefillin transgresses eight positive commandments, etc. — and from the negative you understand the positive, that whoever dons them fulfills eight positive commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:55: Further, he should pursue charity in secret, as it is written (Proverbs 21:14), "a gift in secret pacifies anger." Charity that bears fruit above is charity given for the sake of the Name without any ulterior motive, and if he intends this in the manner of the secret, how good is his portion. And "life" is mentioned regarding charity, as it is said (ibid. 12:28), "in the path of righteousness [charity] is life, and in its pathway there is no death," and likewise (ibid. 16:31), "a crown of glory is gray hair, found in the way of righteousness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:56: Especially on the fast day, it is fitting to give as charity the portion of food that would have been eaten at the morning meal, so as not to gain, through his fast, a reduction in his distribution [to charity]. It seems to me that one may examine this matter precisely in the words of the prophet, who said (Isaiah 58:7), "is it not to share your bread with the hungry" — your own bread, that which would have reached your own portion — to exclude giving the portion of his wife and children, whom he is obligated to support, if he does not have enough to support them except in a strict amount; at least his own portion he should give.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:57: Likewise, he should pursue acts of lovingkindness, as it is written (Proverbs 21:21), "he who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor." And they said in Rosh Hashanah (18a), in these words: Abaye and Rava both came from the house of Eli — Rava, who engaged in Torah, lived forty years; Abaye, who engaged in Torah and in acts of lovingkindness, lived sixty years. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:58: Regarding which comes first, engaging in Torah or acts of lovingkindness, it is explained in the Yerushalmi (Chagigah, ch. 1, halachah 7): Rabbi Yehudah, when he would see the dead and the bride being praised, would set his eyes upon his students and say, deed comes before study. They counted votes in the upper chamber of Beit Arim: study comes before deed. Rabbi Abahu was in Caesarea; he sent his son Rabbi Chanina to give merit [i.e., to eulogize] in Tiberias. They sent and said to him, he is a doer of kindness. He sent a letter to him: is it because there are no graves in Caesarea that I sent you to Tiberias? They have already counted votes in the upper chamber of Beit Arim in Lod: study comes before deed. The rabbis of Caesarea say, this applies when there is someone else there to do the deed, but if there is no one else there to do the deed, deed comes before study. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:59: Further, our sages, of blessed memory, said in the Pesikta, on the verse (Psalms 16:11), "You shall make known to me the path of life" — Rabbi Yudan said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, make known to me the path of life. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, David, do you wish life? Look forward to fear, as it is said (Proverbs 10:27), "the fear of the Lord adds days." Rabbi Ze'ira said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, Master of the universe, make known to me the path of life. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, David, do you wish life? Look forward to sufferings, as it is written (ibid. 6:23), "and the way of life is the reproofs of discipline." Rav said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, make known to me the path of life. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, David, do you wish life? Look forward to Torah, as it is written (ibid. 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it." Another interpretation: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, cast off your astonishment — do and eat, as it is said, "guard My commandments and live." — end of quotation. These four aspects correspond to the four letters of the Name in their order, for one versed in the appellations of the Zohar — and therefore each of these aspects contains "life," in the manner that each letter of the Name includes the whole Name, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Emor 92a), and as my master, may his rest be in Eden, explained in Sefer HaSha'ar, there, regarding the Name of forty-two letters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:60: Further, one should be careful, for what one labors over in his study privately is not quickly forgotten; and so they expounded (Sukkah 49b), "the curves of your thighs are like ornaments" (Song of Songs 7:2) — just as the thigh is [modestly kept] in private, so words of Torah [are best kept] in private — and since one who engages in Torah privately grows wise, behold it is written (Ecclesiastes 7:12), "and wisdom gives life to those who have it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:61: In his reading of Torah he should articulate the words with his mouth, for this leads to remembering and to length of days, as we say in Eruvin (54a), in these words: Shmuel said to Rabbi Yehudah, sharp one, open your mouth [and] read, open your mouth [and] study, so that it be sustained within you and it prolong your life, as it is said (Proverbs 4:22), "for they are life to those who find them [le-motze'ehem], and healing for all his flesh" — do not read "le-motze'ehem" [those who find them] but "le-motzi'eihem" [those who utter them] with the mouth. — end of quotation. This too is especially efficacious.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:62: If he thirsts on the fast day because of the reading, he should consider this an atonement for the sins of idle words, as they said in Tractate Yoma (77a): Rav Nachman said, from here (Jeremiah 2:25), "withhold your foot from being unshod, and your throat from thirst" — withhold yourself from sin, so that your foot not come to be unshod; withhold your tongue from idle words, so that your throat not come to thirst. — end of quotation. And Rashi explained "so that your foot not come to be unshod" as referring to going out into exile — end of quotation. And in this same manner is the thirst — it follows that the thirst of exile atones for idle words, and the same is true of the thirst of a fast that a person accepts upon himself for the atonement of his sin, particularly through engaging in Torah, of which it is written (Proverbs 15:4), "a healing tongue is a tree of life."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:63: Further, he should be careful not to become angry, and should grasp the attribute of humility, explained in the Gate of Humility, where "life" is also mentioned regarding humility, as it is written (ibid. 22:4), "the reward of humility, the fear of the Lord, is riches, honor, and life." Further it is written (Isaiah 57:15), "I dwell in the high and holy place, and with the contrite and lowly of spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and to revive the heart of the contrite." We have already elaborated at length in the Gate of Humility that nothing removes the Shechinah from man, and likewise the soul, except anger, and then it is said of him (Deuteronomy 31:17), "because my God is not within me, these evils have found me" — and in this matter the penitent must be more careful than in everything else.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:64: It says in Sefer Chasidim (siman 649): there was a story of a certain pious man, of whom they asked, by what merit have you lengthened your days? He said, because no person ever cursed me or insulted me that I answered him back — rather, I would bear it and forgive anyone who distressed me. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:65: Further, in Avot D'Rabbi Natan (34:10), they said: ten things are called "life": the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:10), "He is the living God." Torah is called "life," as it is written (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life." Israel is called "life," as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today." The wise are called "life," as it is said (Proverbs 13:14), "the teaching of the wise is a fountain of life." The righteous are called "life," as it is said (ibid. 11:30), "the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life." Gan Eden, as it is written (Genesis 2:9), "and the tree of life in the midst of the garden." Water, as it is said (Genesis 26:19), "living water." The Land of Israel, as it is said (Ezekiel 26:20), "and I will set glory in the land of the living." Jerusalem, as it is said (Psalms 116:9), "I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living." Acts of lovingkindness, as it is said (ibid. 63:4), "for Your kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise You." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:66: All these ten things have practical implications, and although it is not our way in this composition to explain the sayings of our sages, as we prefaced in the introduction, nevertheless we thought fit to explain in general terms what this passage intends, because of the benefits that follow from it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:67: We say that it intends to explain the grades a person needs in order to cling to his Creator, to attain the secret of the supernal life — for He, exalted be He, is the source of life for all existing things, as it is said (Nehemiah 9:6), "and You give life to them all" — and by clinging to Him, a person clings to life, as the liturgical poet said, "and if I cling to You, my life is in my death." Therefore it says that the essential first clinging is to the One who brought everything into being, who is the cause of life for all worlds, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:10), "He is the living God and the everlasting King." And [second], to cling to His Torah, for Torah is the revelation of His Godliness to us, as we shall explain in the next chapter, and He and His Torah are entirely one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:68: Further, that he cling to Israel, because their souls, being holy, flow from the source of the supernal life, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God" — and this is "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are alive" (ibid. 4:4) — meaning, because you cleave to His Name, which is the source of life, as it is written, "He is the living God," therefore you are called "life."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:69: Therefore it is not fitting for a person of Israel to enter into partnership with a gentile idol-worshiper, as explained regarding (Leviticus 25:14), "or buys from your fellow's hand" — and so it is explained in Tractate Megillah (28a), regarding what we say there, it is forbidden to gaze at the image of a wicked man — our sages, of blessed memory, said, Avuha bar Ihi and Binyamin bar Ihi — one said, may this come to me, that I never gazed at a gentile; and the other said, may this come to me, that I never entered into partnership with a gentile. — end of quotation. We have already explained in the Gate of Repentance, chapter 8, that the reason for gazing at the image of a wicked man is that he thereby acquires within his own heart that spirit of impurity that appears in his face, and confusion of thought and nullification of clinging follows from this. Therefore the author of this passage came to inform us that Israel is called "life," so that they engage in business dealings only with Israel, who are called "life," and thereby avoid disturbance of clinging.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:70: Further, that he cling to the wise and the righteous, who are called "life," the intent being that He, blessed be He, dwells within them, and by clinging to them one clings to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:20), "and to Him you shall cling" — and is it possible for a person to cling to the Holy One, blessed be He? Rather, he should cling to Torah scholars; and likewise "the Lord your God you shall fear" (Deuteronomy 10:20) includes Torah scholars (Pesachim 22b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:71: Gan Eden is called "life," to indicate that the essential purpose of clinging to Torah, to the wise, and to the righteous is to merit the World to Come, for the soul's essential dwelling is in the World to Come, where the tree of life is in the midst of the garden, as the first man was before his sin — and one should not perform his deeds or engage in Torah because of any worldly consideration, for then his Torah does not ascend above. And so they expounded in the Zohar (parashat Vayechi, end of p. 223), on the verse (Ecclesiastes 1:3), "what profit has a man of all his labor which he labors under the sun" — it says there, my labor in Torah, which is above [under] the sun. Rabbi Chiya said, even the labor in Torah that one labors for the sake of people, or for his own honor — this "under the sun" is written of it, for it does not ascend above. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:72: Water — of which it is said, "living water" — is also a great cause for clinging, that one purify himself in a mikveh of water; we have already explained and elaborated at length on this in the Gate of Love (ch. 11), regarding "purity leads to holiness" — and especially if the mikveh is of living water, which purifies zavim and zavot, surely it is a greater assistance to clinging.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:73: The Land of Israel — it is known that prophecy rests only in the Land of Israel, and there are several merits to the Land of Israel, one of them being that no outside force has power and providence there, as it is written (Deuteronomy 11:12), "the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it." They said in the Midrash (Shocher Tov), on the verse (Psalms 105:4), "seek the Lord and His strength, seek His face continually" — Rabbi Yosi bar Chalafta said to his son Rabbi Yishmael, do you wish to see the Shechinah in this world? Engage in Torah in the Land of Israel, as it is said, "seek the Lord and His strength, seek His face continually." — end of quotation. And he explained, "seek the Lord and His strength" — Torah is called "strength," as it is said (ibid. 29:11), "the Lord will give strength to His people." "Seek His face continually" refers to the Land of Israel, of which it is said (Deuteronomy 11:12), "the eyes of the Lord your God are continually upon it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:74: Further, on the merit of dwelling in the Land of Israel, it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Acharei Mot 72b), in these words: Rabbi Yehudah said, happy is the portion of one who merits to make his dwelling in the holy land — for whoever merits it merits to draw down the dew of the heavens above that descends upon the land, and whoever merits to be bound in his life to this holy land merits afterward to be bound to the supernal holy land. And he further says: and not only that, but if he merits in his lifetime, he merits to have the holy spirit constantly drawn upon him, while whoever dwells in another domain has another, foreign spirit drawn upon him. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:75: It follows that the essence of clinging to attain the supernal life is in the Land of Israel, particularly in Jerusalem, for the earthly Jerusalem corresponds to the heavenly Jerusalem. There are ten [degrees of] holiness, as explained in the Mishnah (Kelim, ch. 1), and Jerusalem is more sanctified than the Land of Israel and all its surroundings, and according to its holiness so much more flows from it, the clinging to life, for one bound to it — for there is no separating veil between him and the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:76: Acts of lovingkindness are called "life" — for although one engages in Torah, he must also engage in acts of lovingkindness, for this too causes the soul's clinging to the place of life, even though it is outside of reason. Our sages, of blessed memory, said (Midrash Shmuel): it is written, "and Samuel died," and immediately following it, "and a man of Ma'on whose deeds were in Carmel" [Nabal] — the Holy One, blessed be He, said, everyone cries out and beats their chest over the death of the righteous man, and this wicked man sits and holds feasts — to teach you that whoever denies acts of lovingkindness is as though he denies the fundamental principle [of faith]. — end of quotation. Further, on the merit of acts of lovingkindness, they elaborated at length in the Yerushalmi, Pe'ah (ch. 1, halachah 1).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:77: Further, one must conceal his deeds and not reveal them, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Noach 64b), that whoever performs his deeds in secret, blessing rests upon him — and this is in the manner our sages, of blessed memory, explained (see Ta'anit 8b), blessing rests only on something hidden from the eye, in these words: we have learned, the Holy One, blessed be He, is hidden and revealed — "revealed" is the court of judgment below, "hidden" is the place from which all blessings emerge — and therefore all a person's matters that are hidden, blessings rest upon them, and all that are revealed, that is the place the court of judgment rests upon, because it is a revealed place — and all this is according to the supernal secret, in the manner of what is above. — end of quotation.
